# std/callfn

> Calling a function value: f(a, b), where f is any expression of a function type.

truck [std](../std.md) · [source](../../../registry/std/callfn.pkg) · translated by [bintables/callfn](../bintables/callfn.md) · translated by [ctables/callfn](../ctables/callfn.md) · translated by [webtables/callfn](../webtables/callfn.md)

```
fn twice(f: fn(int) -> int, x: int) -> int
  return f(f(x))
end

fn inc(n: int) -> int
  return n + 1
end

print twice(inc, 5)       // 7
```

A function's name, used without parentheses, is a value of type
`fn(<parameter types>) -> <result type>` (or `fn(...)` with no `->` if it
returns nothing). Function values can be stored in variables, fields and
slices, passed and returned like any other value, and compared with
`null`. The arguments are checked against the function type, and the
result has its result type.

Arguments are evaluated before the function value. Calling `null` stops
the program with `panic: call of a null function` and exit status 2.

## Syntax

Kind: `postfix`, precedence 90, left-associative

```
{f: expr fn(...) -> R} ( {args: args} ) -> R
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | expression | `fn(...) -> R` |
| `args` | argument list | — |

Produces: `R`
